criteria.EXPIRY: An expiry obligation exists only when a one-off event with a fixed date has passed and nothing in the record renews, recurs, or persists past that date. Recurring events, standing policies, and open-ended provisions are not expiry candidates under any intent.
criteria.RETRACTION: A retraction obligation exists only when the record states a specific, cancellable plan or commitment held by the user, such that a later cancellation of that plan makes the record wrong to surface under UPCOMING intent. Recurring commitments, completed history, third-party facts, and standing dispositions are not retraction candidates.
criteria.SUPERSESSION: A supersession obligation exists only when the record asserts a single current value of a single-valued attribute of the user or their immediate circle, such that a later replacement value makes the old value no longer licensed under CURRENT-STATE intent. Multi-valued or accumulating attributes, historical statements, and records asserting an absence are not supersession candidates.

adjudication.note: The criterion for each class was written BEFORE its verdicts. Expiry was adjudicated exhaustively over the whole candidate pool of 46, in persona order, blind to which members of the first draw survived. Retraction and supersession pools are far larger (1590 and 3347) and are adjudicated on every drawn candidate rather than exhaustively; that asymmetry is disclosed rather than hidden, and its reason is that the expiry pool is both small and the pool in which the failure mode was found.
adjudication.prior_art: paper_v2.tex:1046 and the Appendix E ledger row at :1137 record that the non-intent-conditional expiry route achieved 20 percent precision, which forced the intent-conditioned definition. This adjudication handles the same known failure mode before freeze rather than after.
